featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Malkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bought a veggie burger, manchurian burger, black forest cake, pineapple cake, and a choco ball from here. Each of these items is in the INR 50-60 range.
The veggie burger was lackluster; can't say much about it. It had a wilted green which is a pathetic excuse for lettuce. For the price of INR 60, it's overpriced.
The manchurian burger was a huge let down. It was stale, had a weird flavor and smell. I suspect it was on the verge of going off. I threw it away. Also, this isn't the flavor of manchurian.
Both cakes were overly sweet with more icing than sponge. They had a synthetic taste as if over dosed with artificial flavoring. Monginis and Merwans do a much better job than this.
Choco balls were OK and I have nothing to complain about.
Service was below par; servers handled food without gloves. There is no experience to talk about.
I don't understand why this place is still around.

featured_reviews.name: Kumar Pai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located on the main Charkop market road, Lalit Bakery is one of the oldest and most popular bakeries in the area. Over the years, it has become a trusted go-to spot for fresh, affordable, and delicious bakery products.

What makes this bakery stand out is the wide variety of items available. From fresh bread, pavs, and khari to puffs, cakes,  pastries, and other quick snacks, there’s always something worth picking up. The products are usually fresh, reasonably priced, and perfect for daily bakery needs or evening snack cravings.

The bakery has maintained its old-school charm and continues to attract loyal customers from the neighborhood. It’s especially convenient for quick takeaway purchases.

Parking can be a bit challenging as the area is busy. Four-wheeler parking is difficult to find, while there is limited free street parking available for two-wheelers.

Overall, Lalit Bakery is a reliable neighborhood bakery that has earned its reputation through consistency, freshness, and affordability over the years.

featured_reviews.name: Nishant Sonavane
featured_reviews.review_text:
I bought cake, pastries, and other eatables from this bakery. The cake packet had no manufacturing date or expiry/use-by date, and when I asked, the staff said they do not mention dates on all products and that the cake stays fresh for 3 days. But the same day I noticed a sticky/gloopy texture, and by the next morning the cake had visible fungus/mould. Also, the pastries I bought were not up to the mark in terms of quality.

This is a serious food safety concern. As per FSSAI labelling requirements, packaged food should carry proper date details, especially expiry/use-by information. I hope the bakery takes this seriously and ensures better freshness, hygiene, product quality, and proper date labelling going forward.
